newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Banco de Colombia has investors guessing.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Colombia has investors guessing.

text.p: Banco de Colombia shareholders approved 1996 financial statements and dividend payments at an annual meeting Friday, but directors of the bank disappointed some market players by failing to shed any light on previously announced plans to form a strategic partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispanoamericano SA.

The meeting was originally set for March 14. It had to be suspended, however, because key members of the Gilinksi family, which own 80 percent of the bank, were still in Europe negotiating the sale of a stake to Banco Central.
Brokers and shareholders had widely expected some sort of a definitve announcement about the merger at Friday's meeting. But the Gilinski family kept them on tenterhooks.
"We're still talking," Isaac Gilinski, who was appointed chairman of the bank's board of directors, told the meeting.
"We've been keeping on top of the negotiations and Colombian authorities have been kept fully informed," he said.
He did not elaborate, but he later told Reuters six or seven points were still outstanding before any deal could be closed.

Under terms of a prelminary accord reached last year, Banco Central would buy anywhere between 25 and 36 percent of Banco de Colombia's voting stock. Little has been said about the deal ever since, however, and Banco de Colombia's local stock has been rangebound -- holding between 420 and 440 pesos -- since January while many of its competitors have been posting solid gains.
Santander Investment and Colombia's Suramericana de Valores brokerage are among those maintaining buy recommendations on Banco de Colombia, which is Colombia's second-largest bank in terms of assets.

"For me, all the thrill has gone from the stock," said Ricardo Arteaga, a broker with Bogota-based Consorcio Bursatil. "The feeling I get is that the merger plans are too vaque and that nothing definitive has been negotiated yet."
Stockholders approved a 14 peso per share dividend at the meeting and an audited balance sheet reporting net income of 51,174 billion pesos in net profits last year against 54,373 billion in 1995.
